analysis:
These changes are to the CI threat-review tooling (.github/scripts/threat_review), not the provider runtime. The only retained threat definition, T-041 (cache), is unaffected. I found no regression against the provider threat-model assets or boundaries, so there are no findings.

bedrock.py adds a 'workload' call policy. plan_calls (lines 69-84) admits the planned count plus one shared repair slot, capped at an emergency ceiling of 500. Exceeding the ceiling raises BudgetStopped, which fails closed. The per-call check at line 122 still enforces self.limit, which stays 0 until a stage is planned. The fixed policy is unchanged. Fallback is still only for explicit decline codes (lines 174-175). Accounting failures still stop all later calls (lines 204-208). Usage and cache-token ledgers are unchanged.

budget_runner.py adds a rerun guard (lines 175-177). A GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT other than 1 raises ReviewFailure inside the try, so the run takes the error path, records errors, and writes a result file with errors. This should block clearance, and it cannot start paid calls. status_body (lines 38-48) now prints an explicit 'Human review required' banner when the review is incomplete and finished or errored. The exception path sets finished=True (line 225).

budget_scan.py replaces the RISK/CRITICAL regex routing with depth_policy.source_depth, which is not in the supplied evidence. Two behavior changes follow. First, cross-file integration findings or needs_deeper_review no longer deepen the whole source set; only batches that cite retained self.findings are deepened. Second, outside force_deep, batches routed to Sol are removed from the Opus list (lines 371-375), so critical files get one deeper pass instead of two.

Open integration questions:
(1) Whether integrate() findings are merged into self.findings. If not, cross-file findings stop driving depth.
(2) Whether depth_policy.source_depth keeps the previous path-based risk and critical coverage, since the module is unseen.
(3) Whether the run() exception handler covers BudgetStopped from plan_calls mid-scan.

The depth reduction is a review-strength trade-off, not a demonstrated vulnerability.
